legacy_source: SESSIONS_DB SQLite sessions, session_events, and approvals tables

backfill.note: Inserts SQLite-only rows into app_sessions, then app_session_events, then app_approvals, in that foreign-key order. Idempotent and insert-only: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, no update path and no delete path, so a row present in both stores but disagreeing is reported as a parity failure rather than overwritten, because PostgreSQL may hold the newer value. Rows the target schema cannot accept are reported with a reason code and never forced: seq <= 0 against CHECK (seq > 0), an event whose session row exists in neither store, a duplicate or already-held (tenant_id, drawing_id), a NULL in a target NOT NULL column, and a consumed-but-undecided approval against CHECK (NOT consumed OR decided). Not yet run against staging: the script reaches the container only through an app image build, and no deploy was dispatched by the lane that wrote it. DEPLOYMENT ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: staging leaves SESSIONS_DB unset, so the legacy source is the task-local server/sessions.db rather than the EFS /data/state volume, and the image is built without it. Deploying the image that carries this command therefore replaces the task and destroys the very source the backfill exists to read, after which every row PostgreSQL retained from BEFORE the deploy classifies as an expected target-only row with no surviving source row to contradict it, and the command is expected to report success without recovering anything (rows written after the deploy land in both stores and match normally, and a fresh post-commit mirror failure is still reported, so that clean result is expected rather than guaranteed). Preserve or export the running task's database BEFORE task replacement, or accept that staging's pre-deploy session history is not recoverable and record that instead. DECIDED 2026-08-06 FOR STAGING ONLY: DISCARD, do not preserve, accepting real loss. Dual-write is NOT fail-closed and this decision does not rest on any claim that it is: the legacy write COMMITS FIRST in session_store.get_or_create_session, append_event and create_approval (each calls its _legacy_ writer before its _pg_ mirror; turn acquire/release and approval decide/consume share the shape) and an unwrapped mirror exception cannot roll it back, so a post-commit pre-mirror failure leaves a source-only row, as test_reconcile_sessions_authority.py documents. _pg_ensure_started and the mirror pre-checks narrow that window, they do not close it. Separately, checkpoints.py and session_policy.py put session_checkpoints and session_policies in the SAME file with no PostgreSQL mirror and no coverage here, so preserving the file would not let this command recover them anyway; under the task-local configuration measured here any task replacement destroys them, which is a property of the current configuration forward rather than a checked history of earlier revisions. What bounds the accepted loss is that the file starts empty at task start and the running task carried dual_write_shadow for its whole life, so exposure is one task-lifetime of staging traffic. Consequence to carry forward: the first staging backfill is EXPECTED to insert nothing, and that expected-empty result is indistinguishable from the post-deploy false-clean, so read it as nothing left to read, never as nothing to recover; a clean staging parity run certifies only agreement since the new task started and is NOT evidence of recovery. Rationale in docs/POSTGRES-CUTOVER.md. Staging-only: must not be reused for production, which sets SESSIONS_DB on durable EFS.

parity.note: Full-data comparison of all three table pairs, not a sampled read. Exits 0 only when every legacy row has a matching target row, 1 with a per-table breakdown when parity fails, and 2 when it could not run. Target-only rows are EXPECTED and never a failure, because staging dual-writes while the command runs. Read-only on both stores by enforcement, not by intention: SQLite is opened mode=ro and the PostgreSQL transaction is READ ONLY at repeatable read. Compares parsed JSON (both sides read as text, since psycopg decodes a JSONB string and a JSONB boolean alike), exact floats (REAL vs DOUBLE PRECISION, matching session_store._shadow_equal's bare !=), and INTEGER 0/1 against BOOLEAN without coercion. Also checks the last_seq == max(seq, 0) invariant over every source session, because both stores can hold the SAME broken state and reconcile happily, then collide on the first turn after the flip. A CLEAN RUN IS NOT BY ITSELF A CUTOVER CERTIFICATE: the two stores are snapshotted separately and the app holds no lock across its dual write, so a legacy commit that lands between the halves, or after the source re-read, is invisible to both. The command detects a source that moved under it (source_stable) and narrows that window, but only quiescing legacy writes closes it. Treat writer quiescence as a required prerequisite of the flip transaction, not of this command. Not yet run against staging: same image-build reason as backfill.

authorities.rollback_mode: Return through shadow or dual_write only while single-task, then select legacy after reverse reconciliation. The two stores have no atomic transaction. Note that shadow is on the RETURN path, not the way forward: shadow is absent from session_store._DUAL_WRITE_MODES, so it stops mirroring to PostgreSQL entirely. Promote dual_write_shadow straight to postgres and never through shadow.

production.evidence: NOT AN OBSERVED SETTING. LEAF_SESSIONS_STORE is ABSENT from production, so the recorded value is the repository default that session_store._store_mode() resolves via os.environ.get('LEAF_SESSIONS_STORE', 'legacy'). Nothing in production was measured to say 'legacy'; only the absence of the selector was measured. Read-only on 2026-08-07 (account 807034087062, us-east-1) from `aws ecs describe-services --cluster leaf-automation-production --services leaf-platform`, which reports task definition leaf-automation-production-platform:98 at desired 1 / running 1, and `aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition leaf-automation-production-platform:98`. The absence was checked across ALL FOUR container definitions (init-platform-data, broker, harness, app) in environment, in secrets, and in environmentFiles (null on every container), so no injection path supplies it. REVISION 98 WILL AGE: a later revision may set the selector, and this record is only evidence about revision 98. CONTRAST WITH STAGING, and it is the opposite posture: production legacy writes NOTHING to PostgreSQL for sessions, so there is no dual-write mirror and no partial coverage to reconcile against. The app container also sets SESSIONS_DB=/data/state/sessions.db on the durable EFS volume rather than leaving it unset, so the legacy source survives task replacement and the full history accumulates there. Any future cutover must therefore backfill the ENTIRE production session history, not a post-deploy remainder, and the staging DISCARD decision recorded in backfill.note must not be reused here.
